steps.title: Sources in, one SD card image out
steps.body:
Read left to right: four pinned source trees plus a root filesystem on the left, the build step for each in the middle, the files each step leaves in `build/deploy/`, and finally the image.

Every column is a step you can also run alone, and `./build.sh --dry-run all` prints the whole recipe with the reasons.

steps.title: Step 1: OP-TEE
steps.body: `./build.sh firmware optee` builds the trusted OS with `PLATFORM=stm32mp1` and the board tree `stm32mp157c-dk2-scmi.dts`. On this 32-bit chip OP-TEE is also the secure monitor and the SCMI server, and it comes out as three files because paging is on.

steps.title: Step 2: U-Boot
steps.body: `./build.sh firmware uboot` builds the bootloader from `stm32mp15_defconfig` for the device tree `st/stm32mp157c-dk2-scmi`. It produces the program and its own device tree, which BL2 needs separately.

steps.title: Step 3: BL2, the only TF-A binary
steps.body: `./build.sh firmware tfa` builds BL2 with an STM32 header the Boot ROM will accept. On this chip there is no BL31, so BL2 is all that is built from TF-A at this point.

steps.title: Step 4: the FIP
steps.body: `./build.sh firmware fip` runs TF-A's `fiptool` to pack OP-TEE's three files, U-Boot and the two device trees into `fip.bin`, a container BL2 can read by UUID.

steps.title: Step 5: the kernel
steps.body: `./build.sh kernel` unpacks the kernel.org tarball, configures it from `multi_v7_defconfig` plus the fragments in `config/kernel/`, and builds `zImage`, the device tree and the modules. It is the longest step.

steps.title: Step 6: the root filesystem
steps.body: `./build.sh rootfs` makes `rootfs.tar` from Debian (mmdebstrap, `armhf`) or Alpine (`armv7`). The packages are 32-bit ARM, so on most build PCs an emulator (qemu) runs their install scripts.

steps.title: The image step stitches it together without root
steps.body:
`fakeroot` and `mke2fs -d` build the ext4 root filesystem from the rootfs and the kernel, `sfdisk` writes the GPT, and `dd` places BL2 twice, the FIP and the filesystem at their partitions.

Nothing here needs root, so you can run it as your normal user.

steps.title: The result: one file to write to a card
steps.body: `sdcard.img` plus a block map that lets `bmaptool` skip the empty parts. `./build.sh flash -d /dev/sdX` writes it, after refusing system disks and asking you to confirm.
